title: Model intake signal routing and enterprise prioritization framework
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a reproducible, signal-driven intake and prioritization framework for model catalog requests (new model adds, version pinning, deprecations, and eval-gate exceptions) with an explicit flow for enterprise customer signals. Goal is to reduce lead time from customer ask -> validated onboarding decision and to ensure enterprise constraints (SLA, data residency, KMS, audit) are surfaced early and consistently.

Why now:
- We have rising volume of ad-hoc enterprise requests that bypass existing intake forms and create inconsistent prioritization and missed compliance checks.
- Ambiguity on when to accept a new model variant vs pin a legacy version has caused regressions for a small subset of enterprise customers.
- Need an operational rubric that links customer signal, technical feasibility, eval results, and commercial priority to an actionable decision (accept / defer / provisional onboarding / blocked).

Scope (non-bug):
- Define signal sources and their routing rules (support tickets, CSM escalations, in-console feature requests, partner integrations, telemetry anomaly detector).
- Create a scoring rubric for triage (enterprise impact, technical risk, performance delta, cost delta, regulatory constraints).
- Formalize evaluation gates (smoke eval, safety scan, latency/cost perf bench, privacy & encryption check).
- Define version pinning policy triggers and deprecation windows for enterprise customers.
- Create templates for engineering intake, PM decision record, and customer-facing response.

Out of scope:
- Implementation of the full intake UI (this ticket produces spec + API contract; engineering will ship UI under ENG-4821).
- Automated enforcement of RBAC and KMS integration (handled in Private product workstream).
acceptance_criteria:
1) A documented routing matrix listing signal sources and the default team route (support, solutions, PM triage).
2) A 5-factor numeric rubric that yields a triage score and recommended disposition (Accept | Provisional | Defer | Block) with example thresholds and rationales.
3) A checklist of eval gates with owners, required artifacts, and pass/fail criteria.
4) Version pinning decision rules that include minimum notice windows and rollback triggers for enterprise customers.
5) Templates (PRD-style) for engineering onboarding request and customer communications.
6) Pilot plan to run the rubric on the next 12 incoming model requests and a plan to measure throughput and stakeholder satisfaction.
7) Linked Confluence spec + GH issue template + two example completed triages for historical requests.
proposed_flow:
1. Signal captured: ticket/CSM/console/telemetry -> tag source + urgency.
2. Auto-enrich: attach customer profile (tier, contract, region), historical model dependencies, prior regressions.
3. Score: apply rubric to compute triage_score (0-100).
4. Route: if score >= 80 -> PM-led deep intake and engineering feasibility; 50-79 -> provisional (must pass eval gates); <50 -> backlog with customer comms.
5. Eval gates: run smoke evals (quality), perf bench (latency & cost delta), and security scan.
6. Decision: Accept/Defer/Pin/Block. Record decision in Model Catalog entry with rollout + canary plan for enterprise customers.
7. Post-mortem: after rollout, measure regression incidents and customer satisfaction.

Owners: PM (triage lead), Eng (feasibility & perf), Security (privacy/KMS), DX (customer messaging).
decision_criteria_matrix:
Factors (weight):
- Enterprise exposure (30%) — number of customers using affected model family and tier.
- Safety/regulatory risk (20%) — new model has unknown safety profile or known red flags.
- Performance delta (15%) — latency and cost per token compared to baseline.
- Implementation complexity (15%) — infra changes, kernel support, quantization needs.
- Commercial value (20%) — upsell retention risk or revenue opportunity.

Example thresholds:
- triage_score >= 80: high priority, schedule dedicated onboarding with SLA negotiation.
- 60 <= triage_score < 80: medium priority, require provisional onboarding with canary customers.
- triage_score < 60: low priority, place in backlog and respond with timeline estimates.
eval_gates:
Mandatory gates before any production onboarding (for enterprise customers):
- Functional smoke eval: qualitative test-suite with customer prompt set; pass = no >5% regression in critical metrics.
- Safety scan: run automated toxicity/adversarial evals; pass = no high-severity failures or documented mitigation plan.
- Performance bench: run 95th percentile latency & cost comparison vs pinned baseline; pass = within agreed SLA delta.
- Privacy & compliance audit: check data residency, encryption keys, and export controls; pass = security sign-off.
- Observability hooks: must include token-level cost attribution and trace IDs for early diagnostics.

Gate owners: Eng (smoke + perf), Research (safety), Security (privacy), PM (sign-off).
version_pinning_policy:
When to pin:
- Customer explicitly requests pinning in contract or ticket.
- New model causes >10% degradation on enterprise critical prompts.
- Regulatory constraints require validated model lineage.

Pinning rules:
- Default pin duration: 90 days, with review at 45 days.
- Emergency pin: immediate pin until root cause/action plan documented (notify accounts + legal).
- Deprecation window: 60 days notice for models scheduled for removal for customers not pinned; for pinned customers offer migration assistance and extended support.

Owner: PM + Customer Success to record pin state in catalog and generate per-customer migration plan.
communication_templates:
- A short customer-facing acknowledgement template (48h SLA) with next steps.
- A technical intake template for engineering that includes required artifacts: model size, weights provenance, license, quantization compatibility, estimated throughput, and cost projection.
- A public deprecation notice template with timelines and recommended migration paths.

Example links: Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/Model+Intake+Signals; GH template: https://github.com/redwood/catlog-templates/pull/47
pilot_plan:
Duration: 6 weeks.
Cohort: Next 12 model requests from mixed sources, with at least 3 enterprise escalations.
Metrics to track: triage lead time (submit -> decision), % of triage decisions changed after eval gates, SLA misses post-onboarding, CSAT for response communication.
Success criteria: reduce median lead time by 40% and achieve >=80% stakeholder satisfaction for pilot triages.
Feedback loop: weekly review with Eng, Security, and Solutions. Update rubric after 2 weeks if >3 decisions overturned.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Rubric under-weights hidden engineering complexity -> Mitigation: required engineering feasibility checkpoint within 5 business days.
Risk: Customers upset by deferrals -> Mitigation: canned comms + optional provisional onboarding for paying enterprise customers.
Risk: Security gating increases lead time -> Mitigation: parallelize safety + perf checks and pre-authorize a fast-track for high-trust customers.
